item.title: edit
item.content:encoded: Changed poisonous to venomous because: “Poisonous—often confused with venomous—means a plant, animal, or substance capable of causing death or illness if taken into the body. item.title: Keeping it safe
item.content:encoded:
What we should keep inside this thing is molds of sessile animals - y'know, stuff like clams and barnacles. So that if it comes to life unexpectedly, it'll just sit there and wait for food particles to swim into its mouth.

That is, assuming there's some reason for us to not keep this thing empty. Is there?

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
From Euclid:
SCPs generally do not stay Euclid for long, as they have high potential of becoming either Keter level objects, or being understood enough to be declared safe.

From Safe:
The designation "Safe" is assigned to subjects that do not display any active hostility to human life, civilization, or the space-time continuum. Safe designates do not commonly require special containment procedures beyond proper storage and cataloging.

As long as you keep it plugged in, it does nothing. If it's unplugged, it's harmless as long as you aren't utterly retarded about which mold you use. Heck, SCP-011 is a sentient, mobile statue with a working rifle and it's designated as Safe.
